title: A second German court treats Google's AI answers as Google's own words
friendlyTitle: A second German court says Google is responsible for its AI answers
summary: The Decoder reports that on 24 September the Aachen Regional Court issued a preliminary injunction after Google's AI Mode attributed another person's criminal case to an Aachen physician. The court treated the generated text as Google's own statement, not as a link to someone else's page, and cited a May ruling from Munich Regional Court I. Google can still challenge the order. The Decoder also reports that Google's announced appeal in the Munich case ended in a settlement, so no higher court has ruled on that reasoning. A breach of the Aachen order can draw a fine of up to €250,000 per violation.
friendlySummary: On 24 September, a court in Aachen ordered Google to stop spreading a false AI answer about a doctor. The system had blamed him for a criminal case that involved someone else. The court said the AI text was Google's own statement, not just a link. Google can still challenge the order. A similar Munich case ended in a settlement, so a higher court has not ruled on the idea yet.
whyItMatters: If you rely on an AI search summary, a German court has again said the company that generated it can be responsible for a false claim about a named person. The order is not final, and it is not a ruling that every AI answer is unlawful. It is a reason to check the source before repeating a serious allegation.
